raw.assessment: The incumbent preassembles rearrangeable parts and checks an order slip, plausibly exposing fit and contents errors before dispatch; effectiveness is unmeasured. Its 11-minute median exceeds the target, five reports suggest contents failures without establishing all five independently, and seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes: a concrete limit on any claim that preassembly necessarily prevents meeting eight minutes. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. Overlapping widths in first-attempt and retried insertions also limit a width-only account. No supplied observation establishes one cause or validates a remedy.

openings.claim: Order switching during selection and checking may contribute to mixed-batch delays and incorrect partitions; complete order-specific staging may reduce both.
openings.delta: Retain preassembly while staging one complete order on a reusable marked board area before insertion.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, staging reduces selection/checking time and contents discrepancies; insertion time remains similar. If only six-compartment insertion stays slow, complexity better explains delays.
openings.probe: Use reversible sample builds, balancing worker, layout and condition order. Compare open-bin work with staged work; time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including staging overhead. Independently reconcile components against each order. Screen within spare-board and available-time limits.
assumptions: Existing geometry, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts and colors remain intact.
Reusable staging stays within 500 initially and 0.40 per order; testing fits delivery slack.

openings.claim: With contents independently verified, does an order-specific slot map resolve uncertainty about the short partition?
openings.delta: Separate instruction ambiguity from actual missing or incorrect contents.
openings.prediction: Fewer placement questions and more unaided successes with the specific map support an instruction contribution; persistent difficulty points toward fit or placement ambiguity beyond the diagram.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants across generic versus order-specific diagrams with matched layouts and verified kits. Record unaided arrangement success and short-partition questions. Treat this small comparison as screening, not proof of the 90% target.
assumptions: Replacement diagrams meet the cost ceiling and delivery date.
Supplied components and ordered configurations remain unchanged.

raw.assessment: Two competing, unverified mechanisms preserve the awkward evidence: partition widths overlap despite insertion retries, and every extreme delay occurred in mixed-layout batches. Layout complexity and switching are confounded; neither cause is established. Customer reports do not establish physical shortages. No proposed mechanism yet demonstrates the pilot targets.

openings.claim: Switching layouts disrupts workers' mapping from partition shape to role, causing selection or orientation corrections. Repetition stabilizes that mapping, explaining faster repeated orders and retries despite overlapping widths.
openings.delta: The bottleneck could be recovering the intended configuration rather than partition dimensions.
openings.prediction: For identical layouts and physical parts, errors and time rise immediately after a layout switch; a temporary order-specific parts-and-placement card reduces that switch penalty.
openings.probe: Use reusable samples across all three compartment counts. Have both workers perform matched repeated and alternating sequences, counterbalancing practice and card use. Separately time selection, insertion, checking, and packing; record orientation corrections, retries, and actual contents.
assumptions: Sample work fits spare capacity before the fixed delivery date.
Temporary sample cards stay within the initial budget; adopting recurring cards requires cost verification.
Mapping difficulty is a hypothesis, including its possible connection to customer confusion.

openings.claim: Insertion difficulty depends on the partition-slot pairing or insertion sequence, which partition width alone cannot capture. Repeated three-compartment orders may avoid difficult interactions; mixed batches may contain harder configurations.
openings.delta: Mixed-batch delay could reflect configuration composition rather than switching costs.
openings.prediction: Retries cluster around particular pairings or insertion stages across workers and persist during repeated identical orders; changing insertion sequence changes retries even without a layout switch.
openings.probe: Reuse the same sample pool, capped at 15 samples across both probes. Identify partitions and slots, then counterbalance insertion sequences within each layout across both workers. Compare recurring difficult pairings with the switch effect measured in A1.
assumptions: Repeated dismantling does not materially change fit; record wear and stop comparisons if it does.
Sequences retain existing parts, footprint, capacity, reversible connections, compartment counts, and colors.
Both mechanisms may coexist; sampled effects do not certify delivery, cost, or customer-success targets.

openings.claim: Switching may disrupt selection/checking or shape-to-role mapping.
openings.discriminator: Staging reduces selection/checking, sparing insertion; placement cards reduce switch-related orientation corrections/retries.
openings.probe: Counterbalance repeated/alternating sequences and staging/card comparisons across workers/layouts; time four stages including overhead; reconcile contents independently.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; reports cannot establish shortages.

openings.claim: Specific slot maps may resolve short-partition uncertainty.
openings.discriminator: Fewer questions/more unaided successes implicate instructions; persistence suggests fit/placement ambiguity.
openings.probe: Compare generic/specific diagrams with ten participants, matched layouts, verified kits.

openings.claim: Pairing/sequence may explain retries despite overlapping widths.
openings.discriminator: Pairing/stage clustering persists under repetition; sequence alters retries without switching.
openings.probe: Identify parts/slots; counterbalance sequences across workers/layouts; compare D1; monitor wear, stopping affected comparisons.
openings.uncertainty: Mechanisms may coexist; dismantling may alter fit.

post_distill.decision: Screen within 15 shared samples and fixed delivery slack. Preserve footprint, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts/colors; verify 500 initial/0.40 recurring ceilings. Repeated-order times keep preassembly plausible. Synthetic evidence establishes no remedy; pilot targets remain unverified.
